subject: Network tolerances & fallback matrix for private deployment
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@ledgercorp.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@ledgercorp.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Apr 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: network tolerances & proposed fallback matrix for LedgerCorp private deploy

Thanks again for your time today — good discussion on the streaming tail behavior and what you need for the initial pilot. This thread captures the core asks, our proposed tolerances, and concrete next steps so your NetOps and our infra team can align.

High-level recap from the call:
- Target latency SLO for streaming tail (95th pct): <= 120ms end-to-end for inference responses at 2 concurrent streams per session.
- Expected steady-state throughput for pilot: ~600 rps across 6 pods (burst to 1k rps for 10s).
- VPN peering preferred; if you must use VPN + NAT, we need static source NAT mapping for port pinning.
- Egress: connections to our inference gateway must allow TLS to redwood-infer-us.prod:443 and a side TCP port 7700 for streaming multiplex backplane.

Proposed tolerances and fallbacks (attached spreadsheet):
- Normal: p95 < 120ms, concurrency per model replica <= 8, KV cache TTL 30s.
- Elevated latency (120-300ms): route to regional fallback model variant with CPU-quantized replica for degraded accuracy but lower GPU contention.
- Severe (>300ms or packet loss >1%): switch to batched HTTP (non-streaming) with client-side buffering for up to 5s.

Action items / owners:
1) LedgerCorp NetOps: provide a 15-minute packet capture from a pilot VM to our team by EOD 4/20 (Sanjay) — format pcap ok.
2) Redwood infra: run synthetic streaming probe from our edge in us-west to your egress IP ranges and share initial latency histogram by 4/20 (Karthik).
3) Security/Compliance: confirm whether LedgerCorp can accept a separate peering tunnel with certificate-based mutual TLS or if you require IPsec/Site-to-Site VPN (Stephanie/Irene).
4) Runbook: we'll draft an egress fallback runbook for your SREs that lists observable thresholds and automated routing toggles (Ben).

Attachments: network-trace-20280419.pcap (stub), slo-tolerance-matrix-ldg.xlsx (proposed tolerances), runbook-egress-fallbacks.pdf (runbook skeleton).

Next call suggestion: quick 30-min NetOps sync on 4/21 at 10am PT to validate captures and confirm peering option. If that works, I'll send calendar invite.

Thanks,

- We can provide the pcap from a staging VM (Sanjay will attach). Expect NAT translation on our side; we can extract the public egress IPs and port mappings.
- For peering: LedgerCorp prefers IPsec S2S today for production, but we can provision a temporary mTLS tunnel for the pilot if Redwood supports cert rotation.
- On the streaming side: our app opens long-lived WebSocket streams. Are you proposing the 7700 port for a separate TCP multiplex, or can that be proxied over standard 443 with ALPN?

Subject: RE: Post-demo: network tolerances & proposed fallback matrix for LedgerCorp private deploy

Liam / Sanjay — quick technical notes from the infra probe we kicked off this morning: 

- Probe summary (first-pass): we ran 1k streaming connections from our us-west edge to the LedgerCorp egress IPs you provided; observed median RTT ~45ms, p95 ~110ms, p99 ~260ms. Packet loss <0.2% for most paths but one ASN hop showed 0.8% loss intermittently. See attached synthetic results link (internal).
- Regarding transport: our streaming stack supports both raw TLS over TCP on a separate port (recommended for lower jitter and pinning) and WebSocket-over-443 with ALPN for environments that cannot open non-standard ports. If LedgerCorp prefers not to open 7700, we can keep everything over 443 but we may see an additional ~8-12ms median overhead in our tests.
- KV cache behavior: to meet the 120ms p95 at your target concurrency we recommend enabling local LRU prefix caching on the gateway and limiting model concurrency to 6 per replica initially. That keeps GPU memory pressure low and reduces tail amplification.

Immediate asks from our infra team:
- Full pcap from staging (Sanjay) + routing table for the egress appliance.
- Confirmation whether LedgerCorp can support static SNAT mapping for the pilot (we map tokens to connection pins).

I'll include the raw probe CSV in the Jira ticket INF-872 and add a heatmap by hop. If anyone on LedgerCorp wants the raw probes, tell me which timeframe to include.

- Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks team — quick alignment and next steps from an ops/runbook perspective.

Decisions we need before pilot kickoff:
- Transport choice: if LedgerCorp confirms IPsec-only for production, pilot will run over IPsec S2S; for the pilot we recommend mTLS over 443 to validate fallback flows (Liam to confirm).
- Port policy: if 7700 cannot be opened, Redwood will default to WebSocket-over-443 and enable additional buffering on our proxy. Expect ~10ms added latency; include that in SLA calculations.

Runbook items I will deliver by EOD 4/21 (attached runbook skeleton):
- Observable thresholds: p95 > 150ms -> shift to regional fallback; p95 > 300ms -> auto-switch to batched HTTP and notify SREs.
- Mitigation playbook: how LedgerCorp engineers can trigger forced failover, drain and revert steps, and where to find debug artifacts (pcap, probe CSV).
- Contact routing: primary NetOps (netops@ledgercorp.com) -> Redwood infra on-call -> product escalation path (Stephanie).

Ben: please prepare the automated reroute toggles and a short rollback checklist. Karthik: drop the probe CSV into INF-872 and link the heatmap in the runbook. Stephanie: please send the calendar invite for 4/21 10am PT.

Irene Choi
